'''Benjamin Chukwukelo Uzoh''' {{Audio|LL-Q33578 (ibo)-Obefelix-Ben Uzoh.wav|Listen|help=no}}(born March 18, 1988) is a Nigerian-American former [[basketball]] player. He played in international competitions for {{bklink|Nigeria}}.<ref>[https://www.vanguardngr.com/2018/02/dtigers-begin-world-cup-qualifier-uganda/ D-Tigers Begin World Cup Qualifier]</ref> Standing at {{height|ft=6|in=3}} and playing at the [[point guard]], Uzoh played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the [[New Jersey Nets]] and [[Toronto Raptors]]. He also played for several teams across North America, Europe, South America and Africa.

==College career==
Uzoh played for the [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane men's basketball|Tulsa Golden Hurricane]] over his four-year [[college basketball]] career.

Uzoh is the only player in school history to be ranked top 10 among points, rebounds, assists, steals and blocks. He's a three time All-Conference USA recipient including his selection to the first team his senior year. He started in 140 games out 141 game in his college career.

==Professional career==
In the summer of 2010, Uzoh earned Portsmouth Invitational Tournament All Third Team.

After going [[undrafted]] in the [[2010 NBA draft]], Uzoh signed a partially guaranteed contract with the [[New Jersey Nets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]]. On January 5, 2011, Uzoh was given a guaranteed contract to play out the rest of the year in New Jersey. He was briefly assigned to the [[Springfield Armor]] of the [[NBA Development League|NBA D-League]], during the month of March 2011.<ref>[http://www.sunherald.com/2011/03/15/2944582/nets-send-uzoh-to-d-league.html Nets send Uzoh to D-League.]{{dead link|date=October 2016 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

In October 2011, he signed a one-year contract with [[PBC Lokomotiv-Kuban|Lokomotiv Kuban]] of the [[Russian Professional Basketball League|Russian League]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/russia/31404/lokomotiv_kuban_announces_ben_uzoh.html |title=Lokomotiv Kuban announces Ben Uzoh. |access-date=2011-10-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111205033614/http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/russia/31404/lokomotiv_kuban_announces_ben_uzoh.html |archive-date=2011-12-05 |url-status=dead }}</ref> but was released after playing just two games.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/russia/32125/lokomotiv_kuban_and_ben_uzoh_part_ways.html |title=Lokomotiv Kuban and Ben Uzoh part ways. |access-date=2011-10-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111231101945/http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/russia/32125/lokomotiv_kuban_and_ben_uzoh_part_ways.html |archive-date=2011-12-31 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On March 27, 2012, he signed a 10-day contract with the [[Toronto Raptors]] of the [[National Basketball Association]].<ref>[https://nationalpost.com/sports/basketball/nba/raptors-sign-ben-uzoh-to-10-day-contract Raptors rule Jerryd Bayless out for season; sign Ben Uzoh to 10-day contract.] </ref> On April 16, 2012, the Raptors announced they had signed Ben Uzoh for the remainder of the 2011–2012 season. He recorded a [[triple-double]] on April 26, against the Nets, the first by a Raptor in eleven years.<ref>[http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=/n/a/2012/04/26/sports/s182745D02.DTL Uzoh has triple-double as Raptors rout Nets.]{{dead link|date=February 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

Uzoh joined the [[Denver Nuggets]] for their training camp in October 2012,<ref>[https://www.nba.com/nuggets/nuggets-announce-2012-training-camp-roster Nuggets announce 2012 training camp roster.]</ref> but did not make the team's final roster.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11273 |title=Denver Nuggets waive guards Anthony Carter, Ben Uzoh. |access-date=2012-10-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150421110155/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11273 |archive-date=2015-04-21 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was then acquired by the D-League team the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/full_list_returning_affiliate_local_tryout_players_2012.html Full List of 2012 Returning, Affiliate and Local Tryout Players Invited to NBA D-League Training Camps.] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151218094230/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/full_list_returning_affiliate_local_tryout_players_2012.html |date=2015-12-18 }}</ref> However, on November 5, 2012, Uzoh was traded to the Armor for [[Tim Ohlbrecht]].<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130130012947/http://www.nba.com/dleague/springfield/armor_acquire_ben_uzoh_2012_11_05.html|title=Armor acquire Uzoh.}}</ref>

On October 31, 2013, Uzoh was acquired by the [[Tulsa 66ers]] in a trade involving the Iowa Energy and the Springfield Armor.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/tulsa/66ers_acquire_no_1_overall_pick_131031.html 66ers Acquire No. 1 Overall Pick and Ben Uzoh] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131204005638/http://www.nba.com/dleague/tulsa/66ers_acquire_no_1_overall_pick_131031.html |date=2013-12-04 }}</ref> On January 22, 2014, he was traded to the Canton Charge.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/canton/news/canton_acquires_uzoh_from_tuls_2014_01_22.html Canton Acquires Uzoh From Tulsa] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222035740/http://www.nba.com/dleague/canton/news/canton_acquires_uzoh_from_tuls_2014_01_22.html |date=2014-02-22 }}</ref> On March 21, 2014, he was waived by the Charge due to a season-ending injury.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/canton/news/charge_reacquire_shane_edwards_2014_03_21.html Charge Reacquire Shane Edwards] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140322115049/http://www.nba.com/dleague/canton/news/charge_reacquire_shane_edwards_2014_03_21.html |date=2014-03-22 }}</ref>

Ben Uzoh went to Nigeria in 2015 where he signed on to play for the Lagos Islanders.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.basketballwithinborders.com/jason-ebie-ben-uzoh-and-william-ndoumbe-combine-for-61-points-against-warriors-on-historic-night-at-landmark-centre/|title=Jason Ebie, Ben Uzoh and William Ndoumbe combine for 61 points against Warriors on historic night at Landmark Centre {{!}} BWB|website=www.basketballwithinborders.com|language=en-US|access-date=2018-07-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180724064328/http://www.basketballwithinborders.com/jason-ebie-ben-uzoh-and-william-ndoumbe-combine-for-61-points-against-warriors-on-historic-night-at-landmark-centre/|archive-date=2018-07-24|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On March 12, 2017, Uzoh signed with Belgian club [[Okapi Aalstar]] for the rest of the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/belgium/228616/ben-uzoh-signs-with-okapi-aalstar.html |title=Ben Uzoh signs with Okapi Aalstar |access-date=2017-03-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170313124932/http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/belgium/228616/ben-uzoh-signs-with-okapi-aalstar.html |archive-date=2017-03-13 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On February 10, 2018, he signed with [[Caballeros de Culiacan]] of the [[CIBACOPA]] league in Mexico.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://gentesinaloa.com/ben-uzoh-se-une-a-caballeros-de-culiacan/ |title=Ben Uzoh se une a Caballeros de Culiacán |language=es |trans-title=Ben Uzoh joins the Caballeros de Culiacán |work=GenteSinaloa.com |date=February 12, 2018 |accessdate=October 19, 2022 |archive-date=May 21, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220521022430/https://gentesinaloa.com/ben-uzoh-se-une-a-caballeros-de-culiacan/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> He earned league All-Star honors.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://cibacopa.org/noticias/todo-listo-para-la-lluvia-de-estrellas-en-culiacan/|title=Todo listo para la lluvia de Estrellas en Culiacán|publisher=[[CIBACOPA]]|date=May 19, 2018|access-date=June 10, 2023|language=es|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201025045555/https://cibacopa.org/noticias/todo-listo-para-la-lluvia-de-estrellas-en-culiacan/|archive-date=October 25, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

On November 24, 2019, Uzoh signed with [[Paris Basketball]] of the [[LNB Pro B]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/paris-basketball-sign-ben-uzoh/|title=Paris Basketball sign Ben Uzoh|last=|first=|date=November 24, 2019|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=November 25, 2019|archive-date=April 23, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200423065644/https://sportando.basketball/en/paris-basketball-sign-ben-uzoh/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On January 20, 2020, [[Paris Basketball]] and Uzoh jointly decided not to continue their collaboration.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketeurope.com/livenews-fr/492842/pro-b-le-paris-basketball-se-separe-de-ben-uzoh/|title=Paris Basketball|date=20 January 2020}}</ref>

In April 2021, Uzoh signed with the Nigerian team [[Rivers Hoopers]] to play in the [[2021 BAL season|inaugural season]] of the [[Basketball Africa League]] (BAL).<ref>{{cite news |title=Rivers Hoopers sign D'Tigers star ahead of Basketball Africa League – AllBallerZone |url=https://allballerzone.com/rivers-hoopers-sign-dtigers-star-ahead-of-basketball-africa-league/ |access-date=April 15, 2021 |work=Allballerzone.com |archive-date=April 15, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210415163614/https://allballerzone.com/rivers-hoopers-sign-dtigers-star-ahead-of-basketball-africa-league/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> He scored the first-ever points in the BAL in the season opener against [[Patriots BBC]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Ben Uzoh scores first BAL points but J. Cole's Patriots bag first win |url=https://www.espn.com/espn/story/_/id/31459554/ben-uzoh-scores-first-bal-points-j-cole-patriots-bag-first-win |access-date=8 December 2021 |work=ESPN.com |date=17 May 2021 |language=en}}</ref> He also became the first ex-[[NBA]] player to play in the newly established competition.<ref>{{cite news |title=Uzoh set to make BAL history |url=https://punchng.com/uzoh-set-to-make-bal-history/ |access-date=8 December 2021 |date=14 May 2021|newspaper=[[The Punch]]}}</ref> The Hoopers were eliminated in the regular season after two losses and one win, with Uzoh averaging a team-leading 14.7 points per game.

In September 2021, Uzoh was on the roster of South African team [[Cape Town Tigers]] and helped the team win its first-ever national championship. He recorded 22 points, 5 rebounds and 5 assists in the championship game against [[Jozi Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite news |title=D'Tigers Ben Uzoh leads Cape Town Tigers to South Africa club championship |url=https://www.premiumtimesng.com/sports/nigeria-sports-news/484227-dtigers-ben-uzoh-leads-cape-town-tigers-to-south-africa-club-championship.html |access-date=14 September 2021 |date=10 September 2021|newspaper=[[Premium Times]]}}</ref>

On July 4, 2022, he signed with [[Marinos B.B.C.|Marinos]] of the [[Venezuelan SuperLiga]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Flores |first=Sairuby Alayon |date=2022-07-04 |title=Ben Uzoh se une al acorazado oriental |url=https://www.liderendeportes.com/noticias/basketball/baloncesto-superliga/ben-uzoh-se-une-al-acorazado-oriental/ |access-date=2022-07-05 |website=Líder en deportes |language=es}}</ref>

== Post-playing career ==
In October 2023, Uzoh became a scout for his former team, the [[Toronto Raptors]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA).<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-10-27 |title=New Raptors scout Ben Uzoh and president Masai Ujiri share more than Nigerian roots |url=https://www.espn.com/espn/story/_/id/38754030/new-toronto-raptors-scout-ben-uzoh-president-masai-ujiri-share-more-nigerian-roots |access-date=2024-01-31 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

==National team career==
Uzoh has played for the [[Nigerian national basketball team]] at the [[AfroBasket 2013|2013]], 2015, and 2017 [[FIBA AfroBasket|FIBA Men's African Championships]]. He was also a member of the Nigerian team that participated at the [[2016 Summer Olympics|Rio 2016 Olympic Games]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.basketballwithinborders.com/ben-uzoh-impressed-with-the-growing-basketball-culture-in-nigeria/|title=Ben Uzoh impressed with the growing basketball culture in Nigeria {{!}} BWB|website=www.basketballwithinborders.com|language=en-US|access-date=2018-07-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180724093138/http://www.basketballwithinborders.com/ben-uzoh-impressed-with-the-growing-basketball-culture-in-nigeria/|archive-date=2018-07-24|url-status=dead}}</ref>
